meta.title: Buy PPL
meta.description: PPL is sold on a public price curve: it starts at $0.005 and rises with every purchase, up to a $0.25 ceiling. The curve closes at $4M raised. Buy and sell at any time.

whyPriceRises.title: Why the price rises
whyPriceRises.noManualLead: The PEOPLE team does not set or raise the price. A public formula in the sale smart contract sets it automatically: each purchase moves the price along the bonding curve. Nobody can change the price manually.
whyPriceRises.mechanism: Same formula-based pricing as Uniswap, Bancor (pioneer, 2017), pump.fun, and Virtuals Protocol on Base: here price = f(tokens sold), transparent and verifiable on chain.
whyPriceRises.example: From the published curve parameters: {startPrice} per PPL at the start, {midPrice} after {midSold} PPL sold (~{midRaised} raised), and {gradPrice} at graduation ({gradRaised} raised).
whyPriceRises.reserve: Funds from purchases stay in the sale reserve on Base and are used to buy PPL back from holders — sell-back for verified users after a 30-day hold, subject to daily limits.
whyPriceRises.chartAria: PPL sale bonding curve: price versus PPL sold

curve.title: One curve, visible to everyone
curve.lead: The price is not set by hand. price = {start} × e^(k·x), where x is millions of PPL sold and k = ln(50)/100. Every figure below is computed from that formula.
curve.ceilingNote: The {ceiling} ceiling is only reached if all {supply} PPL sell. The curve closes first, at {graduation} raised.
curve.capScope: The {ceiling} cap applies during the curve sale only. After graduation to the pool the price is set by the free market — no upper limit and no lower limit.

whatYouGet.title: What a purchase actually gives you

items.title: PPL on your address, immediately
items.body: PPL is recorded to you on the People network the moment you buy. No lock-up on the curve, no waiting list.

items.title: Sell-back from the reserve
items.body: Verified users can sell PPL back to the reserve after a 30-day hold per lot, within daily limits and a {fee} fee. Sell-back closes when the sale graduates. Payouts are in {payoutStable} on {payoutNetwork}.

items.title: Transfers open with the full network launch
items.body: Sending PPL to other people and trading in the pool start at full mainnet: {verified} verified participants, and no later than {months} months.

items.title: At {graduation} the curve closes
items.body: {liquidityShare} of the raise plus PPL at the last curve price seed a public pool whose LP tokens are locked for {lock} months. The other {multisigShare} goes to the project multisig, with public reporting on every spend.

timeline.title: From the curve to a free market

steps.title: The curve
steps.body: {supply} PPL on a public curve from {start} up to a {ceiling} ceiling. Buy and sell at any time, for up to {days} days.

steps.title: Graduation at {graduation}
steps.body: The curve stops. {liquidityShare} of the raise plus PPL at the last curve price go into a public DEX pool at exactly that price, with no jump. LP locked for {lock} months. {multisigShare} to the multisig with public reporting.

steps.title: Full mainnet
steps.body: PPL transfers between wallets and pool trading open at {verified} verified participants, and no later than {months} months.

steps.title: After {days} days
steps.body: If {graduation} is not reached, the same {liquidityShare}/{multisigShare} split applies to whatever was raised, and every unsold PPL goes to the community pool.

faq.title: Questions, answered

items.a: Verified users only: 30-day hold per lot, daily limits, and a {fee} fee. Sell-back closes when the sale graduates.

No. It applies while the curve is running. The curve closes at {graduation} raised, around {graduationPrice} per PPL, below the cap. After graduation the pool price is set by the free market, with no upper limit and no lower limit.

items.q: How do I add the People network to my wallet?
items.a: Use the button below: your wallet is asked to add the PEOPLE network with the official parameters and then switch to it. You can also enter the same values manually from the published network documentation.

items.q: When can I send PPL to someone else?
items.a: At the full network launch: {verified} verified participants, and no later than {months} months. Buying and selling on the curve works from day one.

faq.pumpTitle: What goes wrong on curves without a ceiling
faq.pumpLead: Bonding curves became popular through launchpads like pump.fun. These are their known problems, and what we do instead.

pumpRows.what: The price runs up without limit, so the last buyers before graduation pay many times what the first did.
pumpRows.ours: A hard {ceiling} ceiling, and the curve closes at {graduation} — around {graduationPrice}.

pumpRows.what: Scripts buy in the first seconds from many wallets, then sell to real people.
pumpRows.ours: Up to {perBuy} per purchase, {perDay} per person per day, and a {cooldown}-second pause between trades. If bots show up, the multisig can switch on a verified-only mode.

pumpRows.what: Large holders sell everything at once and crash the price.
pumpRows.ours: Per-person limits stop anyone building a large position. The {fee} sell fee goes to PPL buyback, and pool liquidity is locked for {lock} months.

pumpRows.what: A trade fills at a price much worse than the one you were shown.
pumpRows.ours: Slippage protection on every trade: a minimum received, or the transaction is cancelled.

pumpRows.what: The token is pushed onto exchanges in the middle of the sale.
pumpRows.ours: No listings during the sale. DEX trading only after graduation.

notes.text: PPL is the utility token of the People network. On the curve its price follows the published formula, and after graduation it is set by the market: it can fall as well as rise. PPL is not a security, not a share in a company, not a deposit and not an investment product, and no profit, yield or return of any kind is promised or guaranteed. Figures shown before a purchase are estimates computed from the published formula and are confirmed on-chain before you sign. Nothing on this page is investment, legal or tax advice.
Participation may be restricted or unavailable where you live, and checking the rules that apply to you is your own responsibility. Use only money you can afford to lose.

The AI-assisted reviews named above were carried out by the project team. They are not an audit by an external audit firm; a third-party security audit is completed before mainnet. A bug bounty reduces risk but does not remove it: no review can prove software free of defects.
